title: Accelerating AI-Based Defect Detection in Manufacturing: Synthetic Data and Model Optimization for Rapid and Stable Deployment

abstract: As industrial manufacturing becomes increasingly complex, diverse and unseen product defects frequently emerge. To ensure quality, AI-based image inspection has been widely adopted. Object Detection (OD) models classify defects using human-annotated data, whereas Anomaly Detection (AD) models identify deviations from normal samples without requiring labeled defective data. However, rapid deployment in real-world production remains challenging due to heavy annotation requirements, limited adaptability to new products, and the need to maintain multiple models. We propose a defect detection framework integrating three synergistic approaches. The Synthetic Data (SD) module employs a Domain Randomization (DR) strategy to augment datasets by overlaying annotated defects onto product images with variations in scale, orientation, and appearance. This reduces the need for manually collected defect data and enables OD models to reach high accuracy with fewer real samples. Two AD models are incorporated: (1) the Light Anomaly Detection (LAD) model, designed for rapid deployment and low resource use, builds upon an optimized PatchCore architecture, which reduces memory and computational costs and thus enables efficient training and inference; and (2) the Cross-Product Anomaly Detection (CAD) model, based on EfficientAD, which combines a teacher–student framework with an autoencoder to enhance generalization and detect subtle anomalies. Our experiments show DR with ∼5K substrate defect images improves recall from 82.1% to 93.1% and precision from 82.2% to 93.4%, and reduces the original dataset size by 50%. LAD requires only about 5 minutes of training time using 1K normal 256×256 images, and CAD achieves scalability with an escape rate <0.05%, false positives <1%, and ∼10% uncertain cases. In practice, LAD enables immediate inspection, CAD generalize the inspection ability, and OD retrains with human-labeled anomalies combined with SD for robust classification. This modular workflow accelerates deployment, improves accuracy, and reduces maintenance costs, offering a scalable solution for dynamic manufacturing.
